decision: Adopt std::map (std::less<>) for Snapshot::knobs, SnapshotPatch::knobs, BoolDef::overrides and OverrideTable::values; remove the direct cpp_btree dependency. Hash index and further btree structural repair are not selected.

actual_type_counterexamples.platform: Linux x86_64, g++ 11.2.0 -std=c++20 -O1, ASan+UBSan, global operator new refusing the Nth allocation
findings: Relocation inside full or rebalanced nodes move-constructs pair<const string, V>; the const key is copied, so names longer than the small-string buffer allocate during relocation. A refused allocation there corrupts the table: lost or misordered entries, leaked allocations, and on erase an ASan double-free.

25f9494 insert, long names: Snapshot::knobs and BoolDef::overrides violate contents/leak invariants (41 and 132 violations at max_n 40). Short names (<=15 bytes) never allocate during relocation and pass.
25f9494 erase, long names: all four tables fail (erase refuses an allocation mid-rebalance after removing the entry; ASan double-free). std::map erase never allocates (0 refusals in 480 attempts).
cbc3576 pin additionally publishes a wrong size after a refused nonfull insert (size N+1 != N, 118 to 174 violations per shape at max_n 12), the defect fixed later by bb2ad1d.
patch/cli insert with long names and cli insert with short names did not finish inside the 80 s probe limit at max_n 40; they are not counted as pass or fail.
const_cast in params::swap writes through const keys (language-level UB); no miscompile was demonstrated, and std::map removes the construct.
actual_type_counterexamples.control: std::map arm of the same probe: 0 violations for insert, erase and copy, short and long names.

permanent_regression_test.scope: all four model fields, insert/erase/copy, n=0..24, ordered and shuffled, four positions, short and 200/128-byte names, every refusal position
permanent_regression_test.btree_25f9494: aborts: FAILED content at insert n=3 budget=12 long_names=1
permanent_regression_test.std_map: PASS, 11 s on Linux with unsuppressed LeakSanitizer (two runs); passes in the full local suite

measurement_evidence_reused.source: benchmarks/model-container-comparison-20261022.json (five alternating pairs, macOS x86_64, identical dependency closures, btree 25f9494 vs std::map)
measurement_evidence_reused.reads: int hits within about 6%, bool default/forced reads 10-20% faster, broad misses 17-57% slower (31.1 to 48.8 ms short, 110.4 to 134.5 ms long, per 200k operations)
measurement_evidence_reused.not_rerun: A fresh CPU rerun was not taken: the local host held an exclusive hold for the shared session and the Linux host's strict cores were held by another job. Memory is exact and platform independent; the CPU rows are the accepted October 22 samples.

consumer_qualification.platform: macOS arm64, Apple clang 17, Release, DETENT_BUILD_AUTHORITY=ON, benchmarks off
consumer_qualification.result: clean build with no cpp_btree fetch; ctest 208/208 passed (includes the new test)

compatibility: Four public C++ field types change from btree::map to std::map: layouts (Snapshot 72 to 88 bytes, BoolDef 32 to 48 bytes), iterator types and size_type change. Rebuild every C++ consumer together. Serialized bytes, ordering, duplicate rejection and CLI behavior are unchanged by construction (std::less<>, same call sites).
remaining: Hash index (28.8 MB / 90.4 MB retained, 44-60% faster broad hits) is not selected: no adversarial-key policy and the sorted-publication cost is uncharged.
Byte-identical publication, command digests and mapped images were not re-run beyond the existing suite; run test_snapshot_canonical on the fleet corpus before release.
Incremental cleanup: positional std::map erase is amortized constant; maximum cleanup-turn latency at the supported override limit and allocation-denied authority cleanup are not yet measured.
Larger-system qualification (1.3M primary capacity tier, authority persistent-map and resource-task coordination) is outside this change.
Upstream btree keeps its open const-key relocation defect; document it there rather than repairing it.
